analysis.title: Midday Market Intelligence: hot
key_insights: US stocks are trading lower on Tuesday 11/10/2026 with the VIX back above 20. Drivers are a stronger than expected CPI report, a rise in 10-year Treasury yields, and continued post-Midterms volatility over the past week.

October core CPI came in above expectations at 0.30%, driven by firmer-than-expected readings across a broad set of categories. Headline CPI was also above expectations, helped by the re-escalation of the conflict in Iran.
Front-month Brent oil has fallen 20% since the end of October to $91/bbl. GS reads this as a sign that one underlying driver of the inflation impulse may be receding.

GS cites receding inflation as one underpinning of its solid 2027 consumer spending growth forecast. It also expects tariff effects to wane next year and price pressure in the AI infrastructure supply chain to subside.

The 10-year Treasury yield is up 13bp to 5.00% on the day. Will Marshall's Nov-6 Rates Trader note ('Bonds' Redemption') argues yields can settle into a range and rate volatility can decline. The keys to watch are inflation and growth.

In the AI trade, AVGO and AMD continue to move higher while NVDA and GEV remain under pressure. Investors are assessing how much datacenter shell capacity can be built over the next two years, per Mike Ng's data center capacity notes.

GS forecasts consumer spending growth of 2.2% in 2027 (Q4/Q4), with a slightly softer first half and a pickup as inflation pressures abate. It expects a particular pick-up in the lowest income cohort.
Wednesday is Veterans Day with no major US data releases scheduled. SIFMA recommends that bond markets stay closed.
CRWV, MRCY, STUB, EVLV, GO, BGS, PETS, BV, CARL and others report after the close on 11/10. INVZ, RSKD, FLNG and ODD report before the open on 11/11.

Higher Treasury yields: the 10-year is at 5.00%, up 13bp on the day.
Re-escalation of the conflict in Iran adds to energy and inflation risk.
Uncertainty over how much datacenter shell capacity can be built over the next two years is pressuring parts of the AI trade.

charts_described: Exhibit 1: GS expects consumer spending to grow 2.2% in 2027 (Q4/Q4), with a slightly softer first half reflecting higher rates, elevated energy prices and payback from midterms-related nonprofit spending, then a pickup as inflation pressures abate.

Exhibit 2: GS expects real income growth to become more balanced across the income distribution in 2027, as Social Security cost-of-living adjustments and a partial reversal of benefit cuts lift income in the lower quintiles.
